schema.title: CreateCredentialRequest
schema.description:
Every field is optional. Posting an empty body creates a working credential with a generated
name, a generated password and no file access: safe, but not useful until you set `Permission`
or `HomeDirectoryDetails`.

UserName.description:
The name used to log in. Generated for you when omitted; the generated name is the
credential's `Id`.

Two ways it can be refused, and they differ: a name that is already in use returns `422`,
while a reserved name (`admin`, `root`, `support` and similar) is rejected by validation with
`400`. The name-check endpoint reports both as taken, so check there first if the name
matters to you.

Alias.description: A label for humans, shown in the dashboard. Defaults to the login name.

Permission.description:
What this credential may do with files under its home and chroot directories. Defaults to
`none`, meaning it can connect but sees nothing. Ignored when you send
`HomeDirectoryDetails`, whose folders carry their own permission.

Password.description:
A password of your choosing. It must satisfy your organization's password policy, which
governs its length, the kinds of characters it needs and whether it may appear in a known
data breach. The default policy asks for at least 30 characters, including a number and a
lowercase letter, not found in a breach. No password may be longer than 64 characters. A password that fails is rejected with `400`. Omit
it and we generate one that passes, which is the better option.

HomeDirectory.description:
Where the credential lands after connecting. Defaults to `/home/{UserName}`. Must start with
a forward slash, must not end with one, and cannot contain a variable such as `${...}`.

ChrootDirectory.description:
The highest directory this credential can reach. Defaults to `/`. Set it to the home
directory to confine the credential to its own folder.

HomeDirectoryDetails.description:
Virtual folders, instead of a home directory: the folders the credential sees, each mapped to
a real location in your storage with its own permission. Up to 50.

Each folder must be describable on its own to the web portal, so a very long `Target` can be
rejected with `400`. Many or deep folders together may be too much for SFTP and FTPS; such a
credential is still created, but can sign in only to the web portal, and its
`SupportedProtocols` says so.

items.title: VirtualFolder
items.description:
One entry in a credential's virtual folders: a path the credential sees, mapped to a real
location in your storage, with its own permission.

Entry.description:
The path the credential sees, such as `/inbound`. Must start with a forward slash and must not
end with one, unless it is the root `/`, which must then be the only entry. Entries cannot
share a path or contain one another, and cannot contain a variable such as `${...}`.

Target.description:
The real location in your storage that the entry shows, as a path from the root of your
bucket. Must start with a forward slash and must not end with one. Two entries may show the
same location only if they give it the same permission.

Type.description:
Whether the entry is a folder or a single file. Defaults to `DIRECTORY`. A `FILE` entry
cannot be the root `/`.

Permission.description:
What the credential may do inside this entry. The same levels as a credential's `Permission`,
applied to this entry alone; `none` keeps the entry listed but denies everything in it.

Email.description:
Where web portal invitations and password resets are sent. Leave it out for
machine-to-machine credentials. The address starts unverified; see the email-verification
endpoint.

State.description:
Set to `inactive` to create the credential without enabling it. Anything else is treated as
`active`.

ExpiresAt.description:
When access should stop working, in **Unix epoch seconds**. Must be after the end of today
and no more than a year away. Omit for a credential that does not expire. When the time
passes, the credential becomes `inactive` and its `ExpiresAt` returns to `null`.

typical.summary: A named credential for a specific system

virtualFolders.summary: A partner who drops files in one folder and collects from another

expiring.summary: A drop box that stops working on a date
